title: Progressive serving SDK: idempotency tokens, throttles & fine-grained rollout permissions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build SDK and API primitives to enable progressive model rollouts (canaries, A/B splits, shadowing) with strong idempotency semantics and role-based controls. Focus is on: (1) client helpers that make traffic composition and staged rollouts easy for engineers, (2) server-side idempotency and optimistic concurrency to avoid double-application or partial updates, (3) a minimal permission model so platform teams can restrict who can change traffic weights or trigger auto-rollbacks, and (4) documented failure modes and observability hooks to surface rollout regressions. This ticket coordinates PM requirements, API design, SDK ergonomics, and security review ahead of runtime-1.20.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /api/rollouts with idempotency_token accepts repeat requests and returns the same rollout resource without creating duplicates
API: PATCH /api/rollouts/{id}/traffic supports atomic updates with ETag/If-Match and rejects stale writes with 412 status
SDK: client helpers (Python/TypeScript) provide apply_rollout(), update_traffic(), and pause_rollout() with built-in retry and idempotency token generation
Permissions: two new RBAC checks implemented: rollout.modify and rollout.read; documented and enforced in Console and Private deployments
Auto-rollback: rollout controller triggers rollback when configured SLI deltas exceed thresholds (error rate + latency + hallucination score) and emits webhook + audit log
E2E: integration test that exercises canary -> gradual increase -> auto-rollback path and verifies audit entries and webhooks were emitted
tasks: Draft API spec and OpenAPI snippets for rollout creation, traffic updates, and status endpoints
Prototype SDK helper signatures and publish RFC doc for PD/Eng review
Implement server-side idempotency layer storing idempotency_token -> rollout_id mapping
Add ETag generation to rollout resource and wire If-Match checks on mutating endpoints
Add RBAC checks in private/control-plane and map Console UI actions to permissions
Design auto-rollback policy DSL and integrate with monitoring/eval service
Create integration tests and a small demo app that runs a canary upgrade
Security review and docs for KMS encryption of rollout audit payloads
decisions: Use idempotency_token scoped to organization + caller to avoid cross-org collisions
Adopt optimistic concurrency via ETag rather than serializing all writes to rollout objects to preserve platform throughput
Expose only three traffic operations: set_traffic, adjust_by_delta, and reset to simplify SDK surface
Auto-rollback will be configurable per-rollout with default conservative thresholds (p95 latency + error spike) and an emergency fail-open toggle for safety
Shadow traffic will be implemented by duplicating requests asynchronously to a shadowed model endpoint (no tokens charged to caller) and surfaced as metrics only
blockers: Finalizing the SLI definitions for hallucination score (research/ML to provide signal) - depends on RND-2112
Console permission UI needs one small refactor to show per-team rollout controls (design/console ticket DES-4441)
Agreement on retention period for rollout audit logs in Private (legal/compliance input required)
links: https://observability.redwood/boards/rollouts-2025 - dashboard for canary metrics and regression alarms
